angle: Use AI to scale “read the customer’s email” rituals into daily operating rhythm, not vanity dashboards.
sourceTitle: As Apple gets a new CEO... Tim Cook’s 4 a.m. ritual
linkedinPost:
Customer obsession isn’t a slogan—it’s an operating system.

Fortune recounts Tim Cook’s 4 a.m. ritual: reading hundreds of customer emails for 15 years. That’s not about heroics. It’s about keeping the most important signals close to the work.

Most enterprises try to “scale” this with dashboards that summarize sentiment into green arrows. Then we wonder why the product feels distant from real people.

My take from the field: use AI to scale the ritual, not abstract it. Build a daily, role-specific “customer inbox” that:
- Surfaces raw voice-of-customer snippets tied to real cases/orders.
- Clusters by intent (“can’t find status,” “pricing confusion”), not topic nouns.
- Routes to owners with a suggested fix and a one-click close-the-loop reply.

In customer service, I’ve seen this cut time-to-insight from weeks to hours and drive double-digit deflection because the fix actually matches the frustration.

Before another dashboard, ask: what would your executives learn if they “read the mail” for 15 minutes a day—and how can AI make that unavoidable? #CustomerExperience #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI
xPost: Don’t let AI turn customer voice into green arrows. Build a daily “customer inbox” with raw snippets, intent clusters, and one-click fixes. Scale the ritual, not the dashboard. #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI
